agent.problem: Solomon appears for the first time but is named only as the source of the sayings. Unlike Hezekiah, he is not briefly identified, such as as Israel's king.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

agent.problem: This choice follows another choice card but introduces the new proverb in verse 6 without any setup for it having been told. The baker receives no story-card context before being asked to accept or reject the new assertion.

rule.text: Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

agent.problem: Proverbs 29:17 does not identify the addressees as fathers. Saying "Then he talks to the dads" narrows the audience beyond what the text states.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

human.problem: Stop 1 card 1 cites Proverbs 25:1 to say these sayings are Solomon's, copied by the men of Hezekiah. Every card after that says 'Solomon says.' Proverbs 25:1 introduces 'additional proverbs of Solomon,' but the text never says how far that heading reaches, or that it covers chapter 29.
human.question: Can Papa Dorin treat the Proverbs 25:1 heading as covering chapter 29 and attribute every saying to Solomon? Or should he leave the speaker open, for example by saying 'the proverb says'?
